SENS, the only year-long implantable glucose monitor on the market, reclaimed its own commercial channel on January 1 and stepped gross margin to 59%, with revenue up 87% year over year, the second straight quarter of acceleration. The reason is a lesson in present versus asserted: the margin step is shown today, but the load-bearing growth leg, automated-insulin-delivery integration, is claimed rather than disclosed, with no units and no run rate. The funding overhang is real, a model that needs periodic fresh capital. So the evidence-backed reward sits near two times, and the larger outcome lives only in a low-probability tail. notes.text: Two rejections taught more this week than any of the eight positions we hold. AIRO reached our deep-dive review on the strength of being a genuine counter-drone pure-play in the force we most want to own. Then the load-bearing evidence ran backwards: its order book has declined every quarter since the company came public, and the entire thesis rested on converting a shrinking backlog into rising revenue. A backlog that fades while the story grows is the classic round-tripper signature, the exact tell that separates a name that runs and holds from one that runs and gives it all back. The second name, AUID, never cleared verification. Our survival firewall fired on confirmed going-concern evidence, and a balance sheet that may not last is an automatic no here regardless of how good the narrative reads. The lesson is one rule stated two ways: we buy accelerating operational evidence on a company built to survive long enough to deliver it. Faded evidence and fragile balance sheets are where this book says no. The full screening breakdown is in this week's letter. [LINK]

all_notes.title: The near-miss: SENS cleared due diligence and still did not clear the bar
all_notes.text: One name this week did everything but clear the bar. SENS, the only year-long implantable glucose monitor on the market, reclaimed its own commercial channel on January 1 and stepped gross margin to 59%, with revenue up 87% year over year, the second straight quarter of acceleration. It is taking share in a 15 billion-dollar market two incumbents have held locked at roughly 98%. It completed our full due diligence and earned a constructive read at every turn. The reason is a lesson in present versus asserted: the margin step is shown today, but the load-bearing growth leg, automated-insulin-delivery integration, is claimed rather than disclosed, with no units and no run rate. The funding overhang is real, a model that needs periodic fresh capital. So the evidence-backed reward sits near two times, and the larger outcome lives only in a low-probability tail. GXAI owned a 19.99% sliver of a company that merely licenses counter-drone technology, a weak grade, and it was refused at verification. ASPI sits at the other end. It is held in the earliest, highest-leverage layer of the nuclear fuel chain: the domestic enrichment bottleneck itself, where a legislated supply cliff meets a structural separative-work gap, not a service vendor orbiting it. That is a strong grade, and the position is up 59.0% from 4.22 to 6.71. The grade is not about how good a company is. It is about how directly its revenue rides the force we screened. A strong vehicle in a real force is the whole setup; a weak one is a pass, however hot the headline. [LINK]
